topic: Computing in Ghana: mobile money and society
title: Mobile money at the market
instructions:
## The brief

The Ho Municipal Assembly wants a short, honest analysis of what mobile money has done for traders at Ho Central Market before it decides whether to subsidise digital payments for market stalls.

You have five pieces of evidence: three interviews, a data table and a note on charges. Examine all of them, decide what question matters most, then write your analysis.

A good analysis names benefits **and** costs, says who gains and who loses, and uses the evidence rather than opinion.

nodes.title: Tuesday at the market
nodes.text: You spend a morning at Ho Central Market with a notebook. Examine each piece of evidence, then choose the question you think the Assembly most needs answered.

evidence.title: Auntie Efua, tomato trader, 23 years at the market
evidence.text: "Before, I kept cash in a cloth bag and twice I was robbed on the road to Kumasi. Now my supplier in Kumasi sends the tomatoes when he sees my MoMo. I do not travel with cash. But the charges: every time a customer pays me by MoMo and I cash out, I lose something. On a bad network day I cannot receive at all, and the customers walk to the next stall who takes cash."

evidence.title: Kwame, 24, phone-accessories stall
evidence.text: "All my customers pay MoMo. I keep a record on my phone and I can see what I sold this week. Last month I got a small loan from the MoMo app because they could see my transactions. My mother sells kenkey next to me and still only takes cash; she says the phone menu confuses her and she does not trust the agent."

evidence.title: Mr Dzidzor, MoMo agent at the market gate
evidence.text: "I serve maybe 200 people a day. Cash-outs are more than cash-ins here. When the network is down, people shout at me as if it is my fault. The float I keep is a risk: I have been threatened once. The commission is small per transaction but it feeds my family."

evidence.title: Bank of Ghana figures (summary table)
evidence.text:
| Year | Registered mobile-money accounts (millions) | Value of transactions (GHS billion) |
|---|---|---|
| 2017 | 23 | 156 |
| 2019 | 32 | 309 |
| 2021 | 48 | 978 |
| 2023 | 66 | 1,900 |

About 40% of adults did not have a bank account in 2021; most of them had a mobile-money account.

evidence.title: Note on charges
evidence.text: Operators charge a percentage on cash-outs and some transfers, with a cap. From 2022 a government e-levy applied to many transfers above a daily threshold; it was reduced in 2023 and withdrawn in 2025. During the levy, several traders at the market went back to cash for larger payments.

choices.text: Focus on safety: has mobile money made traders safer?
Focus on cost: do charges and the levy cancel out the benefits for small traders?
Focus on inclusion: who is left out, and why?

nodes.title: Write the analysis
nodes.text:
Write 120 to 200 words for the Assembly. Cover:

- at least two **benefits** with the evidence behind them,
- at least two **costs or risks**,
- **who gains and who loses** (think of Auntie Efua, Kwame's mother and Mr Dzidzor),
- one **recommendation** the Assembly could act on.

prompts.label: Your analysis for the Assembly
prompts.hint: Use the words of the people you interviewed and the numbers from the table.

nodes.title: Submitted
nodes.text: The Assembly's committee reads your analysis alongside two others. Whatever they decide, they now know that a subsidy helps traders like Kwame but does nothing for Kwame's mother unless someone sits with her at the stall and shows her the menu, and that on a bad network day no subsidy matters at all.

hints: Benefits appear in the trader's and the young seller's interviews; costs appear in all three interviews and the charges note.
The table shows scale; the sentence under it shows inclusion.
A recommendation is something the Assembly can actually do: training at the stalls, a shared agent, lobbying on charges, a cash fallback.

checks.label: You examined all five pieces of evidence
The analysis names benefits, costs, winners and losers, and a recommendation
